Note that $\log_{10}\left(x^{3}y^{5}\right)$ can be rewritten using the product and power rules as follows:

$$

$$

Now, since $\log_{10}\left(y\right)=6$ and $\log_{10}\left(x\right)=-5$, we conclude that

$$
3\log_{10}\left(x\right)+5\log_{10}\left(y\right)=3\cdot (-5)+5\cdot 6=15.
$$

$$
\log_{10}\left(x^{3}y^{5}\right)=15.

$$

$$

- $\log_n(c^m)=m\log_n(c)$ - the power rule

$$
\begin{aligned}\log_{7}\left(x^{2}y^{3}\right) &=\log_{7}\left(x^{2}\right)+\log_{7}\left(y^{3}\right) \\ &=2\log_{7}\left(x\right)+3\log_{7}\left(y\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\log_{7}\left(y\right)=2$ and $\log_{7}\left(x\right)=-2$, we conclude that

$$
2\log_{7}\left(x\right)+3\log_{7}\left(y\right)=2\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 2=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\log_{7}\left(x^{2}y^{3}\right)=2.
